result: At exact rmcp-v3.1.4 release source, TaskManager stores task state in Arc<Mutex<TaskManagerInner>> with a HashMap keyed by task_id. get_task, update_task, and cancel_task each lock that mutex, opportunistically sweep TTL state, then address the current entry only by task_id. update_task removes a matching currently-pending input key and ignores unknown/already-answered/superseded keys; TaskContext separately enforces input-request key uniqueness over the task lifetime. cancel_task sets cancel_requested=true and signals the current operation. These operations check no generation, version, expected status/value, CAS precondition, monotonic attempt fence, or historical fence. The stock manager therefore provides current-process serialization and per-input-key replay narrowing, but not a task-wide generation/CAS/history fence. Scope is this exact release and these TaskManager entry points only; no claim is made about application-level fencing outside TaskManager.
